recent-searches.why: A deque adds and removes at both ends in O(1); ArrayDeque does it without per-node allocations. LinkedList works too. ArrayList.remove(0) shifts every element, O(n), harmless for 5 items but the wrong habit. A map loses the natural ordering.

lookup-by-sku.why: HashMap gives O(1) average lookups. TreeMap is O(log n) and only worth it when you need sorted keys. Scanning a list is O(n) per lookup: correct, but far too slow at this volume.

remove-overloads.why: List<Integer> has two remove methods. remove(Integer.valueOf(3)) removes the value 3, giving [5, 8]. remove(0) removes by index, the element at position 0, leaving [8].

map-orders.why: LinkedHashMap keeps insertion order; TreeMap keeps its keys sorted. (A plain HashMap promises no order at all.)

remove-while-iterating.why: The for-each loop's iterator notices the list changed behind its back and throws. Use removeIf, or an explicit Iterator and its remove().

remove-if.why: Collection.removeIf takes a predicate and removes every element it matches, safely and in one pass.

contains-cost.why: ArrayList.contains checks the elements one by one: O(n). Use a HashSet when membership checks are frequent.
